title: DPO: From Preference Pairs to a Policy You Can Explain

articles.title: DPO: From Preference Pairs to a Policy You Can Explain
articles.description: An original visual guide to Direct Preference Optimization: derivation, gradients, token-level implementation, data diagnostics, a runnable PyTorch lab, and the connection to PPO.

articles.title: DPO Starts with a Comparison, Not a Reward Number
articles.description: Understand preference pairs, the Bradley–Terry model, and the offline learning problem before assembling the DPO equation.

articles.title: Deriving DPO: Solve for the Policy, Then Eliminate the Reward
articles.description: Work through the KL-regularized optimum, the partition function, and the reward-to-policy substitution with a three-response example.

articles.title: Read the DPO Loss: Margins, Gradients, and the Two Roles of β
articles.description: Calculate one preference update, understand the reference-relative margin, and distinguish relative improvement from absolute response likelihood.

articles.title: DPO in Code: Score the Right Tokens before Writing the Loss
articles.description: Align causal logits, exclude prompt and padding positions, sum response log probabilities, and build a correctly paired training step.

articles.title: Train DPO with Evidence: Data Coverage, Reference Choice, and Diagnostics
articles.description: Build useful comparisons, understand what offline pairs leave unidentified, and interpret training metrics without confusing them with generated quality.

articles.title: A DPO Lab You Can Verify: Exact Checks and Recorded Training Runs
articles.description: Run the loss and masking checks, fit a finite response policy to synthetic preferences, and compare the learned distribution with an analytic optimum.

articles.title: DPO and PPO: Same Motivation, Different Learning Problems
articles.description: Compare data collection, policy ratios, credit assignment, and evaluation so you can explain precisely what changes when moving between DPO and PPO.
